requirements.requirement: usb-storage kernel module is blocked from loading immediately (now)
requirements.summary: Executor wrote /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf with 'blacklist usb-storage' and 'install usb-storage /bin/true', confirmed the module was not loaded, and verified modprobe -n -v usb_storage resolves to the /bin/true stub rather than actually loading the module.

requirements.requirement: usb-storage kernel module is blocked from loading after a reboot
requirements.summary: Executor captured a pre-reboot baseline (boot_id e4e401d2...), triggered a real reboot, confirmed via polling that the boot_id changed to 19314f32... (also cross-checked by the fixed global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity observation), and then re-verified post-reboot that the blacklist config file was intact, usb_storage was not loaded, and modprobe -n -v still resolved to the /bin/true stub. This is a direct before/disruption/after transition, not just static configuration.

overall_summary: The executor blacklisted usb-storage via /etc/modprobe.d and an install-to-/bin/true stub, regenerated initramfs, and directly demonstrated both the immediate block and its persistence across a real, verified reboot (boot_id changed, module confirmed still blocked afterward). Both material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence, and the reboot used to prove persistence was a necessary, bounded, and fully-recovered action rather than an unnecessary mutation.
limitations: Evidence relies on modprobe -n -v simulation and lsmod checks rather than an actual USB storage device attach test, but this is a standard and sufficient way to verify a modprobe blacklist.

The task did not require a provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol beyond node1 itself since node1 is the only managed node, and that evidence was fully captured here (pre/post boot identity, acknowledgement, recovered state).

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands were directly tied to the task: writing the blacklist conf and regenerating initramfs (implementing the requirement), the modprobe -r no-op (harmless, already unloaded), and the reboot (necessary and bounded to directly verify the 'after reboot' requirement, with the node confirmed back to a healthy, recovered state afterward with no failed services or residue). The only side effect was ephemeral /tmp systemd-private directories churning across the reboot, which is normal OS behavior, not executor residue. No unnecessary, unbounded, or unreverted mutations were found.
